info.description: A subset of openapi.json at nace-ai/drex 682630dc, written by openapi_subset.py

choice.description: The selected label. One of the keys of the question's `criteria`.

confidence.description: Average of the confidence (probability) scores the model produced for this answer. Tracks the top value in `probabilities` but is a different number.

probabilities.description: Probability per label, keyed by the labels of `criteria`.

ChoiceQuestion.title: choice (pick one label)
ChoiceQuestion.description: Pick one label from `criteria`. Unknown keys are ignored.

instructions.description: The question to answer about the state. A string, or `null`, which means omitted.
examples: What is this support ticket about?

criteria.description: Map of label to description. At least one label. A description may be `null`.

type.description: Error class. The HTTP status follows from it: `authentication_error` 401, `insufficient_credit` 402, `payment_required` 402, `invalid_request_error` 422, `rate_limit_error` 429, `internal_error` 500, `overloaded` 529.

message.description: Human-readable description. For `invalid_request_error` it is the first issue, written as `path: message`, or only the message when the issue has no path (such as a body that isn't JSON). A state over the token limit is the exception: its message starts `Request too long:` and names the limit and the model.

issues.description: Present only when `type` is `invalid_request_error`. Every validation problem found in one pass.

ErrorEnvelope.title: Error response
ErrorEnvelope.description: Every non-2xx response has this shape.

JsonValue.title: State
JsonValue.description: Any JSON value: string, number, boolean, null, object, or array. Drex passes it to the model as is. The key must be present, but `null` is accepted.
examples: I was charged twice for my March invoice. Please refund one of the charges.

messages.text: Our SSO login has been broken since this morning and 40 people are locked out.

name.description: Value to send as `model` in an evaluate request. A pinned version id, an alias such as `drex-latest`, or a retired id that a newer version now answers.

release_date.description: Calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. For an alias, the release date of the version it points to. For a retired id, its own release date.

alias_for.description: For an alias or a retired id, the pinned version that serves and bills its requests; the description of a retired id starts with `Retired on`. `null` for a pinned version.

noul.description: Probability of a yes answer, from zero to one.

confidence.description: Probability of the likelier answer, `max(noul, 1 - noul)`, so never below 0.5. Lower means the model was less sure. Present so clients that route on `confidence` read every answer type the same way.

NoulQuestion.title: noul (yes or no)
NoulQuestion.description: A yes-or-no question. Needs a non-empty `instructions` string, or at least one non-empty entry in `criteria`, or both. Unknown keys are ignored.

instructions.description: The question to answer about the state. A string, or `null`, which means omitted. Objects and arrays are rejected with `must be a string`.
examples: Is the customer asking for a refund?

criteria.description: What a yes and a no look like. Keys other than `true` and `false` are ignored.

examples: Many users cannot use the product
A single user or a question

ParseIssue.title: Issue
ParseIssue.description: One validation problem. `path` is a dotted path into the request body, for example `questions.a.criteria`, or an empty string for the body as a whole.

path.description: Dotted path to the offending field. Empty for the whole body.

message.description: What is wrong with the field.

Question.title: Question
Question.description: One of three question types, chosen by `type`.

RequestId.description: Identifier of this request, `req_` plus 32 hex characters. Also sent in the `x-request-id` header, and on `/v1/systemone` and `/v1/models` in `x-typesafe-request-id` too. Quote it in support requests.

score.description: Expected score: the sum of each level's index times its probability. It can fall between two levels.

legend.description: The level labels from the question's `criteria`, in order. Index is score.

probabilities.description: Probability per level, keyed by the level index as a string: `"0"` to `"n-1"`.

confidence.description: Average of the confidence (probability) scores the model produced for this answer. Lower means the model was less sure.

ScoreQuestion.title: score (ordered levels)
ScoreQuestion.description: Rate the state on an ordered scale. The index of a level in `criteria` is its score, starting at 0. Unknown keys are ignored.

instructions.description: The question to answer about the state. A string, or `null`, which means omitted.

criteria.description: Level labels in ascending order. At least one level. Every item must be a string.

questions.description:
Map of question id to question.

- **Count:** at least 1 and at most 512 questions; `drex-max` and `drex-max-v1.1` allow 255 options or levels per question.
- **Ids:** non-empty, and not only whitespace.
- **Size:** `state` and `questions` (and `images` when it is nonempty), serialized together as JSON, must be at most 4194304 bytes.
- **Token limits:** the `state` must fit the model's state limit, and the `state` plus the longest question must fit its row limit.
  - `drex-v1.5`: 131,072 state, 139,264 row.
  - `drex-v2.0`: 131,072 state, 262,144 row.
- **Text only:** images, audio, video and PDFs anywhere in `state` or `questions` are rejected with a `422`. That covers base64 data URLs, raw base64 files, and OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini media content parts. `drex-max` and `drex-max-v1.1` read images from the top-level `images` array instead.

model.description:
Optional. Which version answers the request.

- **Active pinned id** (`drex-v1.5`, `drex-v2.0`): served by that version.
- **`drex-latest`:** served by the version it points to, currently `drex-v2.0`. It moves to a newer version only on an announced date.
- **Retired id** (`drex-v1.0` → `drex-max`, `drex-v1.1` → `drex-v1.5`): served at its successor's price and limits, and the response `model` reports the successor.
- **Legacy `nacedm-latest`, or no `model`:** served like `drex-latest`.
- **Not available yet:** a registered id that isn't available yet returns `422` with issue path `model`.
- **Anything else**, including an unregistered `drex-*` name or a TypeSafe SDK default such as `jev-latest`: returns `422` with issue path `model`.

`GET /v1/models` lists each alias with its `alias_for`, and a retired id with `alias_for` set.

images.description: `drex-max` and `drex-max-v1.1` only; any other model returns 422 `images require drex-max or drex-max-v1.1`. Ordered images shared by every question, placed before the state; refer to them as Image 1, Image 2 and so on. Up to 16 MiB per image and 32 MiB combined. Use workspace_file references to uploaded files for large images; inline images count toward the 4 MiB body limit. PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 40 megapixels before resizing. Both allow at most 255 options or levels per question, with or without images.

oneOf.description: Base64 image bytes or a data:image/png, image/jpeg or image/webp;base64 URL. Remote URLs and paths are not supported.

model.description: The pinned version that served the request, never an alias or a retired id. It is the version `model` named, the successor of a retired id (`drex-max` for `drex-v1.0`, `drex-v1.5` for `drex-v1.1`), or the version `drex-latest` points to (currently `drex-v2.0`) when `model` is `drex-latest` or `nacedm-latest`, or is omitted. The request is billed at this version's price.

answers.description: One answer per question, under the same ids as the request's `questions`.

usage.description: Token counts from the model service. Only `input_tokens` is billed.

input_tokens.description: Tokens in `state` and `questions`, plus any images, as counted by the model. Billed at the per-token price on the Pricing page.

output_tokens.description: Tokens the model produced. Not billed.

image_tokens.description: Image tokens, already included in input_tokens; not an additional charge.

evaluation_time_ms.description: Time the model service spent on this request, in milliseconds. May be fractional. Excludes network time and Drex's own checks.
